adapted_behaviors.rationale: Working-directory and tilde-preserving path expansion near the host filesystem boundary is preserved through repository runtime-path contracts.
Environment-driven path separator expansion at the host filesystem boundary is preserved through repository runtime-path contracts.
Literal tilde filename expansion at the host filesystem boundary is preserved through repository runtime-path contracts.
General command-line expansion that depends on environment and current buffer text is preserved through repository runtime-path contracts.
Shell non-match expansion remains uncovered because repository contracts do not make shell or platform-dependent command expansion a runtime/environment guarantee.
Compound filename re-expansion remains uncovered because it is compound editor-core command-line parsing semantics rather than a dedicated runtime/environment contract.
Runtime loading behavior is preserved through repository-specific runtime discovery contracts.
Path and runtime discovery behavior belongs to adaptation around the host filesystem boundary.
Environment mutation and HOME expansion are observable at the embedded host boundary and are fixed by repository runtime-path contracts.
Escaped globbing near the host filesystem boundary is preserved through repository runtime-path contracts.
Path expansion near the host filesystem boundary is treated as adapted behavior.
optional-feature interpreter dll options remain uncovered because current source builds do not guarantee interpreter-specific option surfaces.
Path-oriented expand() behavior is preserved through repository runtime-path contracts without reimplementing Vim semantics.
Runtime filetype discovery is preserved through runtime-path and runtime loading contracts.
Path and runtime discovery behavior belongs to adaptation around the host filesystem boundary.
Filename and path transformation near the host filesystem boundary is treated as adapted behavior.
Filename and path transformation near the host filesystem boundary is treated as adapted behavior.
Working-directory behavior crosses the host filesystem boundary and is treated as adapted behavior.
Glob-to-regex translation used at the path boundary is preserved through repository runtime-path contracts.
The mapped :global cases remain uncovered because they are editor-core command semantics, not a dedicated runtime/environment contract.
Help and runtime lookup behavior depend on runtime discovery rather than standalone Vim UI ownership.
Help and runtime lookup behavior depend on runtime discovery rather than standalone Vim UI ownership.
Script-context placeholder expansion is preserved through repository runtime-path contracts.
Outside-source placeholder behavior is preserved through repository runtime-path contracts.
Autocmd behavior affects host-visible integration flows and is tracked as adapted behavior.
Filesystem-facing behavior must be mediated by host-side storage contracts.
Channel behavior is preserved through the host-facing job and VFD bridge.

Repository contracts cover a narrow syntax-conceal extraction slice, but they do not justify treating the full upstream conceal file as covered yet. Current public extraction APIs also do not provide stable matchadd conceal parity.
Autocmd behavior affects host-visible integration flows and is tracked as adapted behavior.
Filesystem permission behavior crosses the host storage boundary and is observed through VFS save failure handling.
Filesystem size behavior crosses the host storage boundary and is observed through VFS save request text.
Filesystem change detection is host-owned coordination and remains environment-dependent rather than a dedicated contract.
Filesystem-facing copy behavior is observed through host-mediated VFS save requests and target locators.

Highlight-related behavior is only partially extractable today: search highlight ranges and syntax chunks are covered by search_highlight_contract.rs and syntax_contract.rs, but :highlight definition/resolved attribute tables remain outside the current public extraction APIs, and popup placement/composition stays host-owned presentation policy.
Job requests must be adapted into host-managed process contracts.
Current public extraction APIs do not provide stable matchadd conceal parity yet.
Current public extraction APIs do not provide stable matchadd conceal parity yet.
Menu presentation is host-owned and out-of-scope for a crate-owned extraction contract.
Message behavior is preserved through repository-specific event delivery contracts.

Repository contracts cover popup-menu payload extraction, but they do not justify treating the full upstream popup file as covered. Popup-window presentation remains host-owned rather than a full crate-owned UI contract.

Popup-window behavior is still host-owned presentation: the crate exposes PUM payload extraction, pum stays separate from popupwin exclusion, but no public popup window extractor exists yet, and popup placement/composition/border policy stays in the host rather than the crate contract.

Popup/textprop placement is still a host-owned presentation concern. The repository has no public textprop or popup-window extraction API to bind this case to a crate contract yet, so popupwin is host-owned exclusion, pum stays separate from popupwin exclusion, popup placement/composition stays in the host, and textprop stays the deferred placeholder.
Filesystem-facing recovery behavior must be mediated by host-side storage contracts.
Filesystem-facing rename behavior must be mediated by host-side storage contracts.
platform-dependent path handling is environment-dependent and remains outside a dedicated crate-owned contract.
Filesystem-facing swap behavior must be mediated by host-side storage contracts.
Repository contracts cover specific syntax extraction slices, but they do not yet justify treating the full upstream syntax file as covered.

Text property behavior remains deferred annotation-state extraction today: the deferred placeholder has no public textprop extraction API, so the case cannot be promoted to an extraction contract without a new surface, and any later promotion must define narrow contract-test coverage first.

Additional text property behavior remains deferred annotation-state extraction today: the deferred placeholder has no public textprop extraction API, so the case cannot be promoted to an extraction contract without a new surface, and any later promotion must define narrow contract-test coverage first.
platform-dependent home-directory handling is environment-dependent and remains outside a dedicated crate-owned contract.
XDG and host-environment discovery are observed through the runtime/environment contract boundary.
